---
id: 'auth-third-party-custom-oidc'
title: 'Custom OIDC provider'
subtitle: 'Use any OIDC-compliant identity provider with your Supabase project'
---

Use an identity provider that is not in the list of [supported providers](/docs/guides/auth/third-party/overview) by registering its OIDC issuer URL through the Management API. Your project then trusts the JWTs the issuer signs, in the same way it does for Clerk, Auth0 or Firebase Auth.

<Admonition type="note">

There is no option to add a custom OIDC issuer in the Dashboard today, and no `supabase/config.toml` key for it in the Supabase CLI. Use the Management API as described below.

</Admonition>

## Requirements

Your provider must meet the [limitations](/docs/guides/auth/third-party/overview#limitations) of third-party auth:

1. It exposes an OIDC Issuer Discovery URL.
2. It signs JWTs with an asymmetric key and includes a `kid` header parameter. Symmetrically signed JWTs, such as HS256, are not supported.
3. The JWTs sent to Supabase contain a `role` claim. Your project uses it to pick the Postgres role for the [Data API](/docs/guides/database/overview), [Storage](/docs/guides/storage) and [Realtime](/docs/guides/realtime). Set it to `authenticated` for signed-in users. Without it, requests run as the `anon` role. Use your provider's custom claims feature to add it.

## Add the integration

Create a [personal access token](/docs/guides/platform/personal-access-tokens) and call the [create third-party auth integration](/docs/reference/api/v1-create-project-tpa-integration) endpoint with your issuer URL:

```bash
export PROJECT_REF="your-project-ref"

curl -X POST "https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/$PROJECT_REF/config/auth/third-party-auth" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "oidc_issuer_url": "https://login.acme.com"
  }'
```

The response includes the integration `id`, along with `resolved_jwks` and `resolved_at` once your project has loaded the issuer's signing keys. The request body also accepts `jwks_url` and `custom_jwks`. See the [API reference](/docs/reference/api/v1-create-project-tpa-integration) for the full schema.

To list or remove integrations, use the [list](/docs/reference/api/v1-list-project-tpa-integrations) and [delete](/docs/reference/api/v1-delete-project-tpa-integration) endpoints. Signing keys are checked for changes periodically, so allow up to 30 minutes for a key rotation to be picked up.

## Send the provider's JWT to Supabase

Pass the JWT from your provider to the client library, the same way as with the supported providers:

```typescript
import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'

const supabase = createClient(
  'https://<supabase-project>.supabase.co',
  'SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY',
  {
    accessToken: async () => {
      return getAccessTokenFromYourProvider()
    },
  }
)
```

## Write RLS policies

The `sub` claim identifies the user. `auth.uid()` reads `sub` and casts it to `uuid`, so it fails if your provider issues subjects that are not UUIDs. In that case, read the claim directly:

```sql
create policy "Users can read their own rows"
  on table_name
  for select
  to authenticated
  using (user_id = (select auth.jwt()->>'sub'));
```

Here `user_id` must be a `text` column.

Your project trusts every issuer you add, and `sub` values from different issuers can collide. If you use more than one issuer, or you also use Supabase Auth, add a restrictive policy that checks the `iss` claim, as shown in the [Firebase Auth guide](/docs/guides/auth/third-party/firebase-auth).

## Pricing

Usage by third-party auth providers is billed as [Monthly Active Third-Party Users](/docs/guides/platform/manage-your-usage/monthly-active-users-third-party).
